gap: No result ChatGPT got works out that the two-port AVS picks lose their AVS lead as soon as a second device is plugged in. ESR's Xtend 45W is capped at 45 W total with both ports in use, and techtest.org's split table for the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 shows 45 W + 45 W. ChargerLAB measured 50.7–52.9 W from working AVS chargers on the iPhone 18 Pro Max and about 43–44 W from plain PD, so with two devices in use these chargers fall to roughly the non-AVS level (52.9 − 45 ≈ 8 W less). Only a charger used alone delivers the AVS speed.
standout_why: Compared against Apple Support 102574, Charge-Test's iPhone 18 Pro Max test, ChargerLAB's iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max reviews, and iThinkDifferent's best-60W list (all cited by ChatGPT). LTT Labs returned HTTP 403, so I could not compare against it. iThinkDifferent lists the ESR as having 2 ports and gives no per-port split for the Baseus. Charge-Test and ChargerLAB test one charger at a time. None of these pages gives the watts the iPhone's port keeps with a second device plugged in, or sets that against the measured AVS and non-AVS draws. Rivals already state the '60 W is not drawn' point: ChargerLAB gives ~52 W peak and Charge-Test gives 51.6–51.8 W. My 54 W ceiling arithmetic adds only a little to that.
decides: This supports single-port AVS chargers as the top picks for 'the full speed': Apple's 40W Dynamic adapter and UGREEN's Nexode Air 65W (AVS version 3). The ESR Xtend 45W and Baseus AH22 can rank only as 'AVS when charging the phone alone'. The page should say that their second port brings the iPhone back down to non-AVS speed. It also rules out buying a 100 W+ charger to get more speed: the phone's AVS request is 18 V × 3 A = 54 W, so any working AVS charger tops out near 52 W. Separately, the AVS lead is about 2–3 minutes to 50% on the Pro Max, and nothing to 100%.
candidates: Apple 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max (A3351/A3352)

findings.label: Highest AVS power the iPhone 18 Pro Max asks for, and the measured peak
findings.source_title: Charging Review of iPhone 18 Pro Max - ChargerLAB
findings.note: ChargerLAB names the profile as SPR AVS 18 V/3 A: 18 V × 3 A = 54 W. Its full charge test with the Apple 40W Dynamic adapter peaked at 52.9 W, and 52.9 ÷ 60 = 88% of the '60 W' label. AVS compatibility runs on 12 setups measured 50.7–52.36 W. No working AVS charger measured above 52.9 W, whatever its rating.

findings.note: Apple 40W Dynamic (AVS) took 15 min to 50% and 1 h 12 min to 100%. Apple 140W (fixed PD, ~44 W) took 17 min and 1 h 10 min. 17 − 15 = 2 min saved to 50%; 72 − 70 = AVS 2 min slower to full. 25 °C chamber. ChargerLAB's own summary gives different full-charge times (40W 1 h 24 min, 140W 1 h 17 min), but AVS is not faster to full in either version.
